examples.question_text: A reservoir contains $Q=160+18t-2t^{2}$ megalitres after $t$ days, for $0\le t\le 8$. Find the amount of water and its instantaneous rate of change at $t=3$ days. Interpret the rate.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}Q(3)&=160+18(3)-2(3^{2})\\&=196\text{ ML}\end{align*}$
Differentiate to find the rate.
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=18-4t\\Q'(3)&=18-4(3)\\&=6\text{ ML/day}\end{align*}$
The reservoir contains $196$ megalitres and is filling at $6$ megalitres per day.

examples.question_text:
(a) A tank contains $V=420-\dfrac{96}{t+2}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $t\ge0$. Find its filling rate at $t=2$ hours.
(b) A cyclist's distance travelled is $d=12\sqrt{t}+2t$ metres after $t$ seconds, for $t\ge0$. Find the speed at $t=9$ seconds.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Write the reciprocal as a negative power.
$\begin{align*}V&=420-96(t+2)^{-1}\\V'(t)&=96(t+2)^{-2}\\V'(2)&=\frac{96}{4^{2}}\\&=6\text{ L/h}\end{align*}$
The tank is filling at $6$ litres per hour.
(b) Write the square root as a fractional power.
$\begin{align*}d&=12t^{1/2}+2t\\d'(t)&=6t^{-1/2}+2\\d'(9)&=\frac{6}{\sqrt{9}}+2\\&=4\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A liquid drains from a tank whose volume is $V=240-8t-t^{2}$ litres after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le10$. When is the volume decreasing at $20$ litres per minute?
examples.solution_text:
A decrease of $20$ litres per minute means $V'(t)=-20$.
$\begin{align*}V'(t)&=-8-2t\\-8-2t&=-20\\2t&=12\\t&=6\text{ min}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: The mass of a substance is $M=t^{3}-9t^{2}+24t+20$ grams after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le6$. Find when the mass is momentarily stationary and classify each stationary value as a local maximum or local minimum.
examples.solution_text:
The mass is stationary when $M'(t)=0$.
$\begin{align*}M'(t)&=3t^{2}-18t+24\\3t^{2}-18t+24&=0\\t^{2}-6t+8&=0\\(t-2)(t-4)&=0\\t&=2\text{ or }4\end{align*}$
Use the second derivative to classify these times.
$\begin{align*}M''(t)&=6t-18\\M''(2)&=-6<0\\M''(4)&=6>0\end{align*}$
The mass has a local maximum at $t=2$ hours and a local minimum at $t=4$ hours.

examples.question_text: A tank contains $Q=120-18t+2t^{2}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le4$. Find $Q'(2)$ and $Q''(2)$, including their units. Explain what both values tell you about the water.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=-18+4t\\Q'(2)&=-10\text{ L/h}\\Q''(t)&=4\\Q''(2)&=4\text{ L/h}^{2}\end{align*}$
The volume is falling at $10$ litres per hour. The positive second derivative means the net rate is increasing; the rate of fall is slowing.

examples.question_text: The volume of water in a tank is $V=20+18t^{2}-t^{3}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le12$. Find when the volume is increasing most rapidly and determine that rate.
examples.solution_text:
Let $R(t)=V'(t)$ be the net filling rate.
$\begin{align*}R(t)&=36t-3t^{2}\\R'(t)&=V''(t)=36-6t\\36-6t&=0\\t&=6\end{align*}$
For $0<t<6$, $R'(t)>0$; for $6<t<12$, $R'(t)<0$. The rate increases then decreases, so its maximum occurs at $t=6$ hours.
$\begin{align*}R(0)&=0\\R(6)&=36(6)-3(6^{2})\\&=108\text{ L/h}\\R(12)&=0\end{align*}$
The greatest filling rate is $108$ litres per hour at $t=6$ hours.

examples.question_text: The mass of chemical present is $Q=15t^{2}-t^{3}$ grams after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le15$. Find when the mass is increasing while its net production rate is decreasing.
examples.solution_text:
An increasing mass requires $Q'(t)>0$.
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=30t-3t^{2}\\&=3t(10-t)\end{align*}$
Thus $Q'(t)>0$ for $0<t<10$.
A decreasing net production rate requires $Q''(t)<0$.
$\begin{align*}Q''(t)&=30-6t\\30-6t&<0\\t&>5\end{align*}$
Both conditions hold for $5<t<10$ minutes.

examples.question_text:
A metal plate has temperature $T=18+80e^{-0.2t}$ degrees Celsius after $t$ minutes, for $t\ge0$.
(a) Find its temperature and instantaneous rate of change at $t=5$ minutes, each to $1$ decimal place.
(b) Find when it is cooling at $4$ degrees Celsius per minute, to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}T(5)&=18+80e^{-1}\\&\approx47.4^{\circ}\text{C}\\T'(t)&=80(-0.2)e^{-0.2t}\\&=-16e^{-0.2t}\\T'(5)&=-16e^{-1}\\&\approx-5.9^{\circ}\text{C/min}\end{align*}$
The plate is cooling at $5.9$ degrees Celsius per minute.
(b) Cooling at $4$ degrees Celsius per minute means $T'(t)=-4$.
$\begin{align*}-16e^{-0.2t}&=-4\\e^{-0.2t}&=\frac14\\-0.2t&=\ln\left(\frac14\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/4)}{-0.2}\\&\approx6.9\text{ min}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Q(3)=160+54−18=196 ML. Differentiation gives Q′(t)=18−4t, hence Q′(3)=6 ML/day. The positive rate means the reservoir is filling.
Differentiating −96(t+2)⁻¹ gives V′(t)=96(t+2)⁻², so V′(2)=96/16=6 L/h. Differentiating 12t^(1/2)+2t gives d′(t)=6/√t+2, so d′(9)=2+2=4 m/s. Both evaluation times lie in the stated domains.
V′(t)=−8−2t. A decrease of 20 L/min requires −8−2t=−20, giving t=6 minutes, within 0≤t≤10.
M′(t)=3t²−18t+24=3(t−2)(t−4), so the stationary times are 2 and 4 hours. M″(t)=6t−18 gives M″(2)=−6 and M″(4)=6, establishing a local maximum at 2 hours and a local minimum at 4 hours.

Q′(t)=−18+4t and Q″(t)=4. At t=2, these are −10 L/h and 4 L/h². The negative first derivative means falling volume; the positive second derivative means the negative rate is becoming less negative, so the fall is slowing.
R(t)=V′(t)=36t−3t²=108−3(t−6)². Its maximum on [0,12] is therefore 108 L/h at t=6 hours. Independently, R′(t)=36−6t changes from positive to negative there, and both endpoint rates are zero.

Q′(t)=30t−3t²=3t(10−t), which is positive for 0<t<10. Q″(t)=30−6t is negative for t>5. Intersecting these conditions with [0,15] gives 5<t<10 minutes; endpoints are excluded because the inequalities are strict.

T(5)=18+80/e≈47.4304°C, rounding to 47.4°C. T′(t)=−16e^(−0.2t), so T′(5)=−16/e≈−5.8861°C/min, rounding to −5.9°C/min. Setting T′(t)=−4 gives e^(−0.2t)=1/4 and t=5 ln 4≈6.9315 minutes, rounding to 6.9 minutes.
